findings.evidence: Module.lean:130 `theorem smulRange_le_comap (e : R) (f : M →ₗ[R] N) : smulRange S M e ≤ (smulRange S N e).comap (f.restrictScalars S)`; grep over TauCeti/ returns only lines 54 and 130 of Module.lean. ModuleDecomposition.lean:177-179 proves `rw [mem_vertexComponent_iff, ← map_smul f, vertexIdempotent_smul_of_mem_vertexComponent hx]`, the same argument.
findings.fix: Add `theorem vertexComponent_eq_smulRange (v : Q) : vertexComponent k M v = smulRange k M (vertexIdempotent k v) := rfl` and define `vertexComponentMap` as `(f.restrictScalars k).restrict fun x hx => smulRange_le_comap _ f hx`, dropping the inline `simp only`/`rw` proof.
findings.issue: `vertexComponentMap` re-proves inline exactly the fact `TauCeti.smulRange_le_comap` (Module.lean:130) states — that an `R`-linear map carries `e • M` into `e • N`. Grep shows `smulRange_le_comap` occurs only at its own definition and in the module docstring, i.e. the reusable lemma this PR advertises as "the pieces are natural in the module" is dead while its content is duplicated by the one file that needs it. The obstacle is that `vertexComponent` (line 94) wraps `smulRange` with no bridging lemma, so the general API is only reachable by defeq (as `mem_vertexComponent_iff` at line 100 silently does).

findings.evidence: PathAlgebra.lean:506 `noncomputable def vertexIdempotent (v : Q) : pathAlgebra k Q := ofPath ⟨v, v, _root_.Quiver.Path.nil⟩`; PathAlgebra.lean:484-485 and 510-512 are both `(rfl)`; grep for `ofPath_nil` in TauCeti/ returns no hit.
findings.fix: Add `theorem vertexIdempotent_eq_ofPath (v : Q) : vertexIdempotent k v = ofPath ⟨v, v, _root_.Quiver.Path.nil⟩ := rfl` to `PathAlgebra.lean` (the missing bridge; every downstream user faces the same shuffle) and use `rw [coe_pathMap_apply, ← vertexIdempotent_eq_ofPath, vertexIdempotent_smul_of_mem_vertexComponent x.2]`, closing with `simp` / `LinearMap.id_coe` rather than a bare `rfl`.
findings.issue: `pathMap_nil` converts `ofPath ⟨a, a, Path.nil⟩` into `vertexIdempotent k a` by a round trip `rw [ofPath_eq_single, ← vertexIdempotent_eq_single]` through the `single` normal form, although `vertexIdempotent k v` is *defined* as `ofPath ⟨v, v, Path.nil⟩` (PathAlgebra.lean:506-507), so this is a two-step shuffle between two `rfl` lemmas that breaks on any change to the `single` spelling. The proof then ends in a bare, uncommented `rfl` closing `↑x = ↑(LinearMap.id x)` across the submodule coercion.

summary: The PR adds a general "maps into the piece" lemma and then re-proves it inline downstream, and `pathMap_nil` shuffles through `single` and a bare `rfl` instead of the one-step definitional identity. Everything else is short, robust, and adequately commented.
